extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for petitions to revive abandoned applications, terminal disclaimer requirements, public access to abandoned files, and examiner/applicant interview practice under the MPEP and relevant CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal Disclaimer Requirement (37 CFR 1.137(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(d) requires that a petition under either 37 CFR 1.137(a) or 1.137(b) be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer (and fee) in specified situations (design applications; nonprovisional utility or plant applications filed before June 8, 1995; and certain utility/plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000 where abandonment occurred during appeal, interference, or under a secrecy order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terminal disclaimer must dedicate to the public a terminal part of the term of any patent granted equivalent to the period of abandonment (or, for utility/plant apps filed before June 8, 1995, the lesser of the period of abandonment or the period extending beyond 20 years from the relevant U.S. filing date). It must also apply to patents granted on continuing applications entitled under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c). For utility/plant applications filed on or after May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer is not required due to changes in patent term adjustment rules. Forms PTO/SB/62 and PTO/SB/63 may be used when filing such terminal disclaimers. The Office will not indicate the period disclaimed in its decision granting revival because it cannot determine which period is lesser at that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal Disclaimer Does Not Excuse Intentional Delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a terminal disclaimer is not a substitute for demonstrating that the delay was unavoidable or unintentional under 37 CFR 1.137(a)/(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer cannot excuse an intentional delay in filing a petition or renewed petition to revive an abandoned application. Likewise, an otherwise unavoidable or unintentional delay does not waive the terminal disclaimer requirement of 37 CFR 1.137(d). See Application of Takao, 17 USPQ2d at 1159.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Terminal Disclaimer via 37 CFR 1.183 Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who considers the terminal disclaimer requirement inappropriate may petition under 37 CFR 1.183 (with fee) to request waiver of the 1.137(d) requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver may be requested in toto or to the extent the requirement exceeds the period applicant considers appropriate. Granting is strictly limited to extraordinary situations where 'justice requires' relief (example: abandonment caused no actual delay in prosecution such as when an application awaited a Board decision during the abandonment period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Reconsideration Timing (37 CFR 1.137(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application or lapsed patent must be filed within 2 months of the decision (or within the time set in the decision); this time may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 unless the decision indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a renewed petition, request for reconsideration, or other petition seeking review is filed outside the time specified, the Office may require a specific showing that the entire delay was 'unavoidable' (1.137(a)) or 'unintentional' (1.137(b)). Deliberate decisions by the applicant not to persist in revival (intentional delay) cannot be characterized as unavoidable/unintentional, and subsequent discovery of new information or changes in circumstances are immaterial to such intentional delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival Rules for Provisional Applications (37 CFR 1.137 & 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 applies to provisional applications abandoned for failure to reply to an Office requirement, and any petition must be accompanied by outstanding replies; 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5) provides a provisional is regarded as abandoned 12 months after filing and is not subject to revival after such 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional application may be revived as a pending provisional application for no longer than 12 months from its filing date if delay was unavoidable or unintentional. If a petition is granted later than 12 months from filing, revival can only restore pendency up to the 12-month limit; a provisional will not be considered pending after 12 months from filing under any circumstances. Note: pendency is extended to next business day if the 12-month date falls on a weekend or federal holiday (35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Written Statement on Petition to Set Aside Examiner's Holding (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.181 authorizes the Commissioner to direct an examiner to furnish a written statement within a specified time setting forth the reasons for the examiner's decision upon matters averred in a petition, supplying a copy to the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless such a statement is requested, it should not be prepared. See MPEP § 1002.01 for additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access to Abandoned Applications (37 CFR 1.14 & ordering conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to an abandoned application may be provided to any person, subject to 37 CFR 1.14(i), if a written request for access is submitted and if the abandoned application is not within the file wrapper of a pending continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) and is referred to one of the permissible categories (e.g., in a U.S. patent/publication; in another U.S. application open to public inspection; or in an international application published pursuant to PCT Article 21(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of specification, drawings, and papers may be provided upon written request and payment of fees (see 37 CFR 1.19(b)(2)). Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access under 37 CFR 1.14(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulling and Forwarding Abandoned Application Files
rubrics_metrics.description: Files of abandoned applications are pulled and forwarded to the Files Repository on a biweekly basis one month after the full 6‑month statutory period has expired (the date of abandonment is after midnight of the date the shortened statutory period, including any extensions under 37 CFR 1.136, expired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must carefully verify applications are actually abandoned and check files for Board decisions with allowed claims to avoid erroneous forwarding. Patented and abandoned files are stored at the Files Repository or off-site warehouses; drawings are generally stored within application file wrappers and delivered with the file. Files are ordered via a PALM transaction and the PALM response indicates acceptance status (accepted; accepted but stored off-site; not accepted because file not located; not accepted because previous request not yet filled; not accepted because number invalid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying Applicants of Abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps mails a Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432 to the correspondence address of record in all applications becoming abandoned for failure to prosecute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to receive the notice does not affect the status of abandonment. Applicants should act promptly upon receiving notice; lack of prompt action may preclude relief. If non-receipt of Office action or notice is alleged, consider possible problems with correspondence address and consult MPEP § 402 and § 601.03 regarding change of address procedures. File a paper notifying the Office of any address change promptly in each application (with exceptions for Customer Number practice per MPEP § 403).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Abandonment Received After Application Allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: An express abandonment arriving after the issue fee has been paid will not be accepted without a showing of one of the reasons indicated in 37 CFR 1.313(c), or a showing under 37 CFR 1.183 justifying suspension of 37 CFR 1.313.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt of a letter of abandonment while an application is allowed is acknowledged by the Publishing Division; see MPEP § 711.01 for related authority and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and Citation of Abstracts, Abbreviatures, and Defensive Publications as Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications (published Official Gazette materials) are publications and may be cited as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) effective from their date of publication in the Official Gazette. Defensive publications are prior art only as of their publication date (not as of filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application or portion thereof from which an abstract, abbreviature, or defensive publication was prepared may be used as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) effective from the actual U.S. filing date. These publications may be used alone or in combination with other prior art to reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103. Defensive Publications are listed with 'U.S. Patent Documents'; Abstracts and Abbreviatures are listed under 'Other References' per the citation formats provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Permitted Timing of Interviews (37 CFR 1.133)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview is the personal appearance of an applicant, attorney, or agent before the examiner or a telephone/video/email exchange presenting matters for the examiner’s consideration. Interviews concerning patentability must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours; an interview for patentability will not occur before the first Office action unless the application is a continuing or substitute application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may require scheduling; interviews are permissible on any working day except during overtime; Internet e-mail shall NOT be used to conduct interview-type exchanges unless written authorization is given to use internet e-mail, and a paper copy of internet e-mail contents must be placed in the application file per the Federal Records Act. Interviews must be arranged in advance normally, and VCC/video interviews must be requested with required lead times (e.g., 3 days for VCC; 1 week for video tape viewing arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-Initiated Interview Request and Preparation (PTOL-413A & PTOL-413)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant initiates an interview, an Applicant Initiated Interview Request form (PTOL-413A) should be submitted in advance to permit the examiner to prepare and focus on issues to be discussed; a copy of the completed request should be attached to the Interview Summary form PTOL-413 at completion and a copy given to the applicant or representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should identify participants, proposed date, interview medium (personal/telephone/video), and include a brief description of the issues. An interview should be used to develop and clarify specific issues and to advance prosecution; applicants should be fully prepared (preferably provide a proposed amendment in advance). Examiners should avoid unnecessary interruptions and manage scheduling; appointments should be kept and substitute arrangements made promptly when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct Limits and Purpose of Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews should be held only when they can develop and clarify specific issues and lead to a mutual understanding to advance prosecution. The parties share responsibility to keep interviews to a reasonable period, usually not longer than 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should identify issues and attempt to resolve differences; may conclude an interview if no common ground or further action needed. Examiner may grant one interview after final rejection (see MPEP § 713.09). If agreement is reached, applicant should promptly submit amendment per agreement; if amendment prepares case for final action, examiner should take case up as special. Consideration of filed amendment may be advanced by hand delivery of duplicate copies and prompt communication of results to applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Pre-Action and 'Sounding Out' Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing, no interview is permitted except limited discussion of the field of search; requests for interviews prior to first Office action are ordinarily granted only in continuing or substitute applications; interviews solely to 'sound out' an examiner are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unexpected appearance without prior notice may justify refusal. Search in the Technology Center art unit should be permitted only with consent of the primary examiner. The USPTO will not act as an expounder of patent law or as counselor for individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Make Substance of Interview of Record (37 CFR 1.133(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement of the substance of any face‑to‑face, video conference, electronic mail, or telephone interview with regard to the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement was reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In every instance where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview must be filed by the applicant. An interview does not remove the necessity for reply to Office actions per §§ 1.111 and 1.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Conference Center (VCC) and Video Tape Viewing Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's Video Conference Center (VCC) is available to expedite prosecution; video conferences must be arranged in advance and use of VCC is limited to authorized official business and listed PTDL locations. Attorneys wishing to show video tapes during interviews must demonstrate the tape bears on an outstanding issue and prior supervisory approval is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VCC interviews must be arranged in advance (at least 3 days); requests to use video viewing equipment should be made at least 1 week in advance. The substance of the interview, including a summary of the video tape content, must be made of record. Scheduling of rooms and equipment is done by the examiner through Patent Academy personnel, not by applicants directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Interviews When Examiner Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner who conducted an interview is transferred or replaced, the new examiner should ascertain whether any agreements were reached at the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where conditions permit (absence of clear error or other prior art), the new examiner should take a position consistent with agreements previously reached. See MPEP § 812.01 for telephone practice in restriction/election situations.
